source_text: III. Igitur apprehensis nobis et apud [regionantes — sense unclear: local officials?] in custodia constitutis, sententiam praesidis milites nuntiare audivimus, quod heri corpus nostrum minaretur urere. nam, ut postea quoque verissime cognovimus, exurere nos vivos cogitavit. sed dominus, qui solus de incendio servos suos potest liberare, in cuius manu sermones et corda sunt regis, furentem a nobis saevitiam praesidis avertit. et incumbentes precibus assiduis tota fide statim quod petivimus accepimus: accensus paene in exitum nostrae carnis ignis extinctus est et flamma [caminorum — scan cammorum] ardentium dominico rore sopita est. nec difficile credentibus fuit nova posse ad vetera exempla pertingere, domino per spiritum pollicente quia qui gloriam istam operatus est in tribus pueris, vincebat et in nobis. IV. Tunc a proposito suo domino repugnante confractus, mitti nos in carcerem iussit. quo deducti a militibus sumus, nec expavimus foedam loci illius caliginem; moxque carcer tenebrosus spiritu perlucente resplenduit, et contra obscuritatis deformia et caeca nocte contecta instar diei fidei devotio candida luce nos vestiit. et ad summum ascendebamus locum poenarum quasi ascenderemus in caelum. quales illic dies duximus, quales transegimus noctes, exponi nullis sermonibus possunt; tormenta carceris nulla affirmatione capiuntur, nec veremur atrocitatem loci illius ut est dicere. quo enim temptatio grandis est, eo maior est ille qui eam vincit in nobis. et non est pugna, quia est domino protegente victoria. nam et occidi servis dei leve est, et ideo mors nihil est, cuius aculeos comminuens contentionemque devincens dominus per trophaeum crucis triumphavit. sed et nulla causa armorum est nisi quando miles armandus est, nec armatur nisi quando congressio est; et in coronis nostris ideo praemium est quia certamen ante praecessit, nec datur palma nisi congressione perfecta. sed paucis diebus visitatione fratrum refrigeravimus; nam omnem noctis laborem diei solatium laetitiaque abstulit.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: we were seized and held in custody before district officers and heard soldiers report the governor's verdict threatening to burn our body; he had in fact meant to burn us alive. The Lord who alone rescues his servants from burning, who holds a king's speech and heart in his hand, deflected his raging cruelty. Persisting in unceasing prayer in full faith, we immediately obtained the request: the fire lit nearly to kill our flesh went out and the flame of the hot ovens was quieted by the Lord's moisture. Believers readily held that recent events can match ancient models, as the Lord pledged by the Spirit that the one glorified in the three lads would win in us too. Then, thwarted in his plan by the Lord's resistance, he sent us to prison. Brought by soldiers, we did not fear the foul murk; the gloomy jail soon gleamed with the Spirit shining through, and devout faith dressed us in bright light like daylight against the ugliness of darkness and night-blind cover. We climbed to the topmost punishment place as toward heaven. No speech can state what days and nights we lived there; no statement contains prison pains, yet we do not shrink from naming that place's harshness. Where trial is large, the one beating it in us is larger. No fighting remains where the Lord's guard gives triumph. Being slain is slight for God's servants, so death is nothing, because the Lord crushed its stings, mastered its struggle, and triumphed by the cross-trophy. Arms exist only for arming a soldier, and arming only for combat; crowns hold prize because combat came first, and palms require finished combat. After a few days brothers' visiting revived us, for day's consolation and gladness removed night's whole burden.
pass_b_english: Therefore, after we were seized and placed under guard before the local officials, we heard the soldiers announce the governor's sentence, that he was threatening to burn our body; for, as we afterward learned most truly, he had planned to burn us alive.
But the Lord, who alone can free his servants from the fire, in whose hand are the words and the hearts of the king (Prov 21:1), turned the raging cruelty of the governor away from us.

And as we pressed on in constant prayers with whole faith, we at once received what we asked: the fire kindled almost to the destruction of our flesh was extinguished, and the flame of the burning furnaces was laid to rest by the dew of the Lord (Dan 3).

Nor was it hard for us as believers that new deeds could reach back to the old examples, since the Lord was promising through the Spirit that he who worked this glory in the three youths would also conquer in us (Dan 3).
Then, broken from his purpose because the Lord opposed him, he ordered us to be thrown into prison.

Led there by the soldiers, we did not dread the foul gloom of that place; and soon the dark prison shone bright as the Spirit shone through, and against the deformities of the darkness and things covered by blind night, the devotion of faith clothed us as with daylight in white light.
And we were going up to the highest place of punishments as if we were going up into heaven.

What days we spent there, what nights we passed through, cannot be set forth in any words; the torments of the prison cannot be grasped by any declaration, nor do we fear to speak of the savagery of that place as it is.
For where temptation is great, greater is he who conquers it in us.
And there is no battle, because with the Lord protecting there is victory.

For even to be killed is a light thing to the servants of God, and therefore death is nothing, since the Lord, shattering its stings and defeating its strife, triumphed through the trophy of the cross.

But there is no reason for arms except when the soldier must be armed, nor is he armed except when there is an encounter; and in our crowns there is a reward for this reason, that a contest went before, nor is the palm given unless the encounter is completed.
But after a few days we were refreshed by the visitation of the brethren; for the comfort and joy of the day took away all the toil of the night.

choices.term: in cuius manu sermones et corda sunt regis
choices.english: in whose hand are the words and the hearts of the king
choices.why: manu is ablative of location with in, and sermones et corda is plural subject with sunt, so the king's speech and heart are both held by the Lord
rejected: in whose hand is the speech of the king's heart

choices.english: was laid to rest by the dew of the Lord
choices.why: dominico rore is ablative of means with sopita est, a divine cooling that quenches the furnace flame rather than ordinary water
rejected: was put to sleep by morning mist

choices.term: instar diei fidei devotio candida luce nos vestiit
choices.english: the devotion of faith clothed us as with daylight in white light
choices.why: instar diei is adverbial like daylight, while candida luce is ablative of means and nos is direct object of vestiit
